{{Recipe}}

'''Kunun gyada''' is a light porridge made from blended raw groundnut and rice, usually eaten in the northern part of Nigeria. It is similar to ''[[Cookbook:Akamu (Nigerian Pudding)|akamu]]'', except that blended rice is poured into a boiled groundnut milk when the later is made by pouring pap into boiled water. The type of soft rice variety used in making kunun gyada is that used in making [[Cookbook:Tuwo Shinkafa (Nigerian Mashed Rice)|tuwo shinkafa]].

== Ingredients ==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] raw [[Cookbook:Groundnut|groundnuts]]
*½ cup soft [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
*⅓ cup cool [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Tamarind|tamarind]]

== Equipment ==
*[[Cookbook:Blender|Blender]]
*[[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|Pot]]
*[[Cookbook:Spatula#African turning stick|Turning stick]]
*[[Cookbook:Cooktop|Stovetop]]

== Procedure ==
# Soak the tamarind for 3 hours and extract the juice. Also, soak the rice and raw groundnut in separate bowls for a few hours.
# Drain the groundnuts. Grind them in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] with some water and [[Cookbook:Straining|strain]] the resulting groundnut milk.
# Drain the rice and grind with a little water.
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the groundnut milk in a pot, stirring to prevent sticking and lumps. Slowly stir in the blended rice.
# Stir in the tamarind juice and serve.
